newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM'S NOKIA SALE INVITES PROFIT-TAKERS.
newsitem.headline: UPM'S NOKIA SALE INVITES PROFIT-TAKERS.

text.p: Shares in Finnish telecoms group Nokia, powering this week to new all-time highs, may come in for profit-taking after forestry group UPM-Kymmene sold a large chunk, brokers said on Thursday.

"There could be profit taking today simply because of the recent sharp rise," one broker said after UPM announced the sale of 4.5 million shares. Nokia stock in Helsinki has risen by over seven percent this week alone.
UPM's chief financial officer Jan-Henrik Kulp said the shares had a book value of 40 markka each: UPM said on Wednesday it made a 1.5 billion markka capital gain on the deal.
Some brokers expected Nokia to start trading around its Wall Street closing level which would equal about 380 markka, some 11 markka below its Helsinki close of 393 markka.
But others, calculating the price UPM would have fetched, saw a sharper fall to around 370 markka. The calculation would price UPM's Nokia stock at around 373 markka.
"When Nokia went over 390 markka I think it went above the target price of the Finnish houses," said one analyst, requesting anonymity.
He saw UPM's decision to sell about 40 percent of its Nokia holding as "some kind of selling signal. UPM has seen that the price has so long been so high that it was a good time to sell."
"But I would not over-emphasize the significance of this deal," he said.
The broker said he expected Nokia's gains to calm down -- at one stage this week market operators had a further spurt to 440 markka in their sights -- but he saw support at 350 markka.
Smith Barney on Wednesday disclosed new targets for Nokia and Ericsson, seeing Nokia at $114 over 18 months which at current exchange rates would be over 580 markka.
"I think that in the recent sharp rise there has been 53 percent fundamentals, 47 percent rumour," the broker said, pointing to Nokia's continued strong growth prospects.
-- Eeva Prunnila, Helsinki newsroom +3589 6805 0247, e-mail news@reuters.fi
